title: Marked semistable alteration over an arbitrary excellent base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant morphism of excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] schemes, with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $y$ of $Y$, and suppose the generic fibre $X_y$ is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] curve. Let $Z\subset X$ be a nowhere-dense closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose generic fibre $Z_y$ is finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] over $\kappa(y)$, possibly empty. Then there are integral excellent Noetherian schemes $X_1,Y_1$, alterations $a:X_1\to X$ and $b:Y_1\to Y$, and a morphism $f_1:X_1\to Y_1$ with $fa=bf_1$. The morphism $f_1$ is proper, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are nonempty connected reduced curves of pure dimension $1$, smooth except at ordinary double points, and its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral. There are an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset X_1$ in the relative smooth locus and a nowhere-dense closed subset $T_1\subset Y_1$ such that $D\to Y_1$ is proper etale, $f_1$ is smooth over $Y_1\setminus T_1$, and $a^{-1}(|Z|)\subseteq |D|\cup f_1^{-1}(T_1)$. An ordinary double point has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ on a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. An alteration is proper surjective and finite over a dense open of its integral target.

source.place: Exposé IX, Theorem 1.2 (i), (iii)--(vi), p. 131; no separatedness or projectivity hypothesis on Y; trivial-group specialization of weak de Jong 2.4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-stein-smooth-generic-curve] to $f$, obtaining $X\xrightarrow{g}S_0\xrightarrow{q}Y$. Put $K=\kappa(y)$ and $L=\kappa(\eta_0)=H^0(X_y,\mathcal O)$, where $\eta_0$ is the generic point of $S_0$. The cited node says that $L/K$ is finite separable; it does not say that the function field of the curve is finite over $K$. The latter has transcendence degree one. The finite relative-spectrum description gives $(S_0)_y=\operatorname{Spec}L$, so associativity of fibre products identifies $X_{\eta_0}$ with $X_y$ as schemes, endowed with its canonical $L$-structure. Its smooth geometric integrality is supplied by the Stein node. Regard $Z_y$ with the induced $L$-structure: its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the original finite etale morphism. Since $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale], cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](3) makes $Z_y\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ etale. It is finite: its finite-dimensional $K$-algebra is also finite-dimensional over $L$ (the same generators suffice). This works also for the zero algebra, hence the empty marking.

source.place: Exposé IX §1.3, p.132, Stein reduction; distinguish the constants field from the curve function field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to the proper map $g:X\to S_0$. The Noetherian base is qcqs, so [det-chow-projective-closed-immersions] applies to its proper surjection $\pi:T\to X$, projective-space immersion, and dense isomorphism open $W=\pi^{-1}(V)\simeq V\subset X$. The two projective-space immersions are closed. The scheme $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $T\to S_0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Thus $W\hookrightarrow T$ is quasi-compact. Let $C_0$ be its scheme-theoretic image, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $W\subset C_0$ is open and dense. On any affine chart meeting $C_0$, its coordinate ring is the image of restriction into sections on the nonempty open of the integral $W$, hence is a subring of its function field and a domain. Thus $C_0$ is reduced and irreducible, hence integral. Its closed inclusion into $T$ shows that $C_0\to X$ is proper and birational and $C_0\to S_0$ is projective.

source.place: Tag 0200, lemma-chow-Noetherian; scheme image: morphisms.tex Tag 01R8, and the cited immersion-open-in-image node.

proof.text: The generic fibre $(C_0)_{\eta_0}$ is integral: on affine charts it is a localization of a domain, and its dense open is $V_{\eta_0}$, a nonempty open of $X_{\eta_0}$. Thus its proper map to $X_{\eta_0}$ is birational. Both have the same function field, so [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg], applied to each entire curve over $L$, gives dimension one for $(C_0)_{\eta_0}$. The smooth curve $X_{\eta_0}$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. All schemes here are separated and finite type over $L$ by properness. Hence [lem-trf-proper-birational-normal-curve-iso] makes the generic-fibre map an isomorphism. Pull the finite etale marking of Step 1 back through this isomorphism and let $H_0$ be its schematic closure in $C_0$.

source.place: Tags 0AB7, 0BFP and 0B1C; generic marking through the resulting isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flatification-horizontal-curve-pair] to $(C_0,H_0)\to S_0$. The base is excellent integral Noetherian, $C_0$ is integral and projective, its generic fibre is the smooth integral curve of Step 3, and $H_0$ is the closure of its finite etale generic marking. Obtain an excellent integral Noetherian $S_1$, a birational blowup $v:S_1\to S_0$, and strict transforms $C_1,H_1$. The curve $C_1\to S_1$ is projective, flat and finitely presented with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres; $H_1\to S_1$ is finite flat finitely presented of pure dimension zero when nonempty. Their generic fibres are unchanged, $C_1$ is integral, and $C_1\to C_0$ is proper birational.

Apply [lem-trf-stable-modification-flat-curve-pair] to $(C_1,H_1)\to S_1$. Step 4 verifies flatness, finite presentation, the pure relative dimensions, the closed marking, and smooth/etale generic fibres. Obtain an excellent integral Noetherian $S_2$, a projective dominant generically finite $r:S_2\to S_1$, and compatible maps $m:X_1\to C_1\times_{S_1}S_2$ and $n:D\to H_1\times_{S_1}S_2$, both generically isomorphisms. Here $m$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense, $n$ is proper, $f_1:X_1\to S_2$ is flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one with nodal geometric fibres, and $D$ is closed in $X_1$, etale over $S_2$, in its relative smooth locus. Set $Y_1=S_2$; the intermediate base remains denoted $S_1$ throughout.

source.place: Exposé X §3.2.2 and Theorem 3.4 Step 3 and first sentence of Step 4, pp.158,160–161.

proof.text: The generic isomorphisms in Steps 3–5 identify $(X_1)_{\eta_2}$ with $X_{\eta_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}L}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta_2)$. It is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). It is geometrically integral by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]: after every further field extension it is still a field base change of the geometrically integral $X_{\eta_0}$. No separability of $\kappa(\eta_2)/L$ is used.

source.place: Exposé X Theorem 3.4, proof, base-change observation preceding Step 1.

proof.text: We now prove integrality of $X_1$, which is not asserted by the stable-modification node. Over any affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S_2$, let $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X_1$ be a nonempty affine open mapping into it. Restrict flat $f_1$ and apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with the trivial invertible module. Every nonzero $a\in A$ acts injectively on $B$, so $B\to B\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}A$ is injective. The localization is nonzero and is the coordinate ring of a nonempty affine open of the integral generic fibre from Step 6, hence is a domain. Therefore $B$ is a domain. This also proves that every nonempty such affine open meets the generic fibre, so that fibre is dense in $X_1$. Its irreducibility makes its closure $X_1$ irreducible, and the domain charts make $X_1$ reduced. Thus $X_1$ is integral.

source.place: Flat-generic restriction argument (lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, torsion-free argument); written for an arbitrary domain.

proof.text: Finite presentation of $f_1$ implies finite type. Since $S_2$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X_1$ Noetherian. Cover $S_2$ by excellent affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and their inverse images by affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite type over $A$. By [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] with multiplicative set $\{1\}$ each $B$ is excellent. The affine-cover theorem [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] makes every affine coordinate ring of $X_1$ excellent, which is the required scheme excellence. Thus both $X_1$ and $Y_1=S_2$ are integral excellent Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent; Noetherianity: morphisms.tex 01T6; affine-cover locality: morphisms.tex 0HAB.

proof.text: Set $b=qvr:S_2\to Y$ and $a$ equal to $X_1\xrightarrow m C_1\times_{S_1}S_2\to C_1\to C_0\to X$. Compatibility gives $fa=bf_1$. The base change of projective $C_1\to S_1$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-base-change] and [lem-pc-projective-proper]. The morphism $m$ is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. Thus $f_1$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The blowup $v$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $q$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and $r$ is proper by projectivity. The projection $C_1\times_{S_1}S_2\to C_1$ is a base change of proper $r$. Together with the proper maps in Steps 2–4, proper composition proves $a,b$ proper. Their images contain the respective generic points: on generic curves $a$ is the projection of a finite field base change, and $b$ is dominant. Their images are closed, so both are surjective. The generic fibre of $b$ is finite because $r$ is generically finite and $v$ birational, while $q$ is finite. Over the generic point of $X$, the map $a$ has fibre the spectrum of $k(X)\otimes_L\kappa(\eta_2)$, a finite-dimensional algebra over $k(X)$; hence this fibre is finite. Proper maps are qcqs and locally finite type, and both targets are Noetherian. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood] supplies dense opens over which $a,b$ are finite. They are alterations.

source.place: Tags 01W3–01W5, 01WC and 02NW, assembly of the alteration square.

proof.text: The proper image $f_1(X_1)$ contains the generic point of $S_2$ by Step 6, hence is all of $S_2$; every geometric fibre is therefore nonempty. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-proper-component-count-lower-semicontinuous] to the proper flat finitely presented $f_1$. Every open neighbourhood of a point $s\in S_2$ contains its generic point, so lower semicontinuity gives $n(s)\le n(\eta_2)=1$. Nonemptiness gives $n(s)\ge1$, hence all geometric fibres are connected. They are pure one-dimensional by Step 5. At a smooth point they are reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Each geometric fibre is finite type over a field, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. At an ordinary double point its Noetherian local ring $R$ injects into its completion by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson], applied to its maximal ideal and $M=R$. The completion $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ embeds into $\Omega[[u]]\times\Omega[[v]]$ by restriction to the axes (a series vanishing on both is divisible by $uv$), and each factor is a domain by its lowest nonzero coefficient. The completion and its subring $R$ are reduced. Thus all geometric fibres are reduced nodal curves.

source.place: Exposé IX Theorem 1.2(iv); reducedness expanded via Stacks 00IQ, connectedness via 0BUI.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], the relative smooth locus $U\subset X_1$ is open and contains $D$. The smooth curve $U\to S_2$ has relative dimension one by Step 5. Since $D\to S_2$ is etale, it is flat, unramified and locally finitely presented by [def-weil-etale-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] makes it locally quasi-finite. Applying [lem-pc-cartier-criterion], implication (3) to (2), to its closed immersion in $U$ makes it a relative effective Cartier divisor there. Since $D$ is closed in $X_1$ and disjoint from $X_1\setminus U$, its ideal is the unit ideal off $D$; the Cartier property therefore holds on all of $X_1$. Furthermore $H_1\times_{S_1}S_2\to S_2$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Its composition with proper $n:D\to H_1\times_{S_1}S_2$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Thus $D\to S_2$ is proper etale.

Let $T_{\mathrm{sing}}=f_1(X_1\setminus U)$. It is closed by properness and omits the generic point by Step 6. Put $E=a^{-1}(|Z|)$. It is closed in the Noetherian $X_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c) and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], its reduced closed subscheme is Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components] gives finitely many components. On the generic fibre $E$ equals $|D|$ by the pair isomorphisms. If a component dominates $S_2$, its generic point lies over $\eta_2$ (the generic point of the image closure is the image of the generic point); thus its generic point belongs to closed $|D|$, and the entire component is contained in $|D|$. Let $V$ be the union of the remaining components. Their proper images are closed and omit $\eta_2$, so $T_{\mathrm{vert}}=f_1(V)$ is a proper closed subset. Set $T_1=T_{\mathrm{sing}}\cup T_{\mathrm{vert}}$. This finite union is closed and omits the generic point of the integral base, hence is nowhere dense; $f_1$ is smooth over its complement and $a^{-1}(|Z|)\subseteq |D|\cup f_1^{-1}(T_1)$. Empty markings and empty vertical unions satisfy the same argument.

source.place: Exposé IX 1.2(iv),(vi), p.131, and Exposé X Theorem 3.4 Step 8, p.161, horizontal/vertical decomposition.

split_report.summary: Repair of all four defects at returned head 94f364e361: distinguish the finite constants field from the curve function field; explicitly prove X_1 integral using flat-generic injection, and Noetherian/excellent using finite type and affine-cover locality; declare the generic Chow tools and other off-unit inputs; and give the new properness node its full blueprint ancestry. Intermediate bases are named S_0,S_1,S_2 consistently. Reducedness, nonemptiness and properness of both alteration maps are also explicit.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the arbitrary-base marked alteration route in lem-trf-local-term-locality, proof of (1)--(2): Stein reduction; Chow and flatification; stable modification; assembly and boundary construction.

tool_uses.why: General Chow projectivization over the excellent Noetherian base, retaining a dense isomorphism open; supports the existing semistable route and is not a substitute for it.
Upgrades the two immersions in Chow data to closed immersions for a proper morphism over a qcqs base; no node of this unit gives that generic projectivization fact.
General dimension/function-field calculation for the birational generic curve; the trace unit gives no replacement.
Generic smooth-curve normality used only to apply the birational-isomorphism lemma.
Flat sections over a domain have no base torsion; used with O to prove X_1 integral, not to bypass the alteration construction.
General ring permanence makes the finite-type affine coordinate rings excellent.
General finite-projective-space base-change permanence in assembly of the square.
General properness of finite-projective-space projective morphisms.
General properness of the finite-type-ideal blowup supplied by horizontal flatification.
General conversion of finite generic fibres to finiteness on a dense open for proper maps to Noetherian targets.
Only smooth morphism base-change permanence is used, to retain the smooth generic curve.
Generic proper-flat-family component-count theorem converts the geometrically integral generic fibre into connected fibres.
General smooth-field-fibre reducedness, used at smooth points of geometric fibres.
Generic relative-Cartier criterion on a smooth relative curve, used for the etale closed marking.
General finite-map base-change permanence proves the finite projection used for marking properness.
General unramified-to-locally-quasi-finite implication supplies the hypothesis of the Cartier criterion; the etale definition alone does not state it.
